interpretation.graphics: Guest uses Microsoft Subsystem GLES translator; current WsaClient has package gfxstream/ANGLE and NVIDIA ARM64 D3D UMD modules loaded, with nonzero raw 3D/Copy engine counters. This supports an active host GPU path rather than a purely CPU-only stack.
interpretation.graphicsLimit: Does not prove every app draw is GPU accelerated, the exact active D3D backend, frame pacing or 120 FPS.
interpretation.refresh: The live Windows internal-display change to 120 Hz did not change the already-running WSA virtual display modes from 60 Hz. This establishes the current live behavior, not a permanent WSA 60 Hz cap.
interpretation.internal120: DISPLAY1 2880x1800 was successfully tested with a temporary 120 Hz mode. WSA guest display 2 and FrameProbe draw callbacks stayed about 60 Hz; both Windows displays were restored to their original full DEVMODE values.
interpretation.external120: DISPLAY2 3440x1440 enumerates only 60 Hz under the current connection and resolution.
